Keep engagement context separate

Agency work moves among inboxes, project tools, creative reviews, specialist platforms, and Slack. Start each Maia task in the client's working channel and name the records it may use for that engagement.

Begin with a named client workspace, a defined set of sources, and clear channel membership. The account lead decides what the client may see, while the delivery team keeps internal notes in the right place.

Turn intake into a usable brief

Provide the client request, signed scope, approved brand guidance, deadline, and any required source assets. Maia can extract the deliverable, audience, constraints, dependencies, missing inputs, and open questions.

The result is a creative or project brief plus proposed tasks. Account and delivery owners confirm scope and priority before work begins. An ambiguous request should become a client question, not an invented interpretation.

Prepare a weekly client update

Give Maia the project export, recent decisions, selected performance data, and the reporting period. It can draft completed work, next milestones, blockers, client dependencies, and decisions needed, with links back to the records.

The account lead edits and approves the external wording. Performance claims need their source, metric definition, and date range. Maia should not infer campaign attribution or business impact from a partial dashboard.

Catch scope questions early

When a new request arrives, Maia can compare it with the described deliverables in the signed statement of work and quote the relevant section. It can prepare an internal note and a neutral clarification for the client.

The account owner decides whether the request is in scope, whether to change fees or timing, and how to handle the relationship. Maia does not make a contractual judgment.

Follow through after meetings

From approved notes or the meeting thread, Maia can extract decisions, owners, dates, client dependencies, and unresolved questions. It can compare them with the project record and propose exact task changes.

The meeting owner approves the recap and any external send. Proposed tracker changes remain visible before creation, which helps prevent a loose discussion from becoming an unintended commitment.

Start with one client channel

Choose one engagement with a signed scope, an incomplete request, and a small project export. Ask Maia to cite the scope, leave the open question with the account owner, and draft the client update for editorial review.

After the account lead resolves the open question, Maia can draft the project update and client recap from the same decision. The team sees how the request changed the plan, and the client receives a clear statement of next steps after review.

Questions from agency teams

Can each client have separate guidance and memory?

Configure each client channel with its own approved context and rules. Keep channel membership and connected access aligned with the engagement.

Can clients work with Maia in a shared channel?

External-channel use needs a deliberately limited audience and capability set. Begin with internal preparation until that setup has been reviewed.

Does Maia replace the project tool?

No. Maia brings project context into Slack and can propose updates. The project system remains the operational record.
